blocks.x: Agentic AI & Hyperautomation applied to Corporate & Investment Banking. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

CIB margins compress while deal complexity grows: origination research, credit memos, trade documentation and risk reporting all consume expensive analyst hours that agentic systems can compress — with the control discipline investment banks cannot compromise.

items: LCs, trade documents and settlement instructions fail on reference mismatches; exception queues run through time zones.
Pitch books, credit memos and research notes re-type data from terminals and filings; quality varies by analyst stamina.

blocks.x: The pattern composes Process & Task Mining, Autonomous Workflow Orchestration, Intelligent Document Processing from the Agentic AI & Hyperautomation tower, wired into the unit's workflows (Credit memo production, Trade document handling, Intraday risk aggregation) on Dataq Swarm and Dataq Nexus and Dataq Compass. Governance inherits the sector frame — Basel capital regimes among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: One automation spine: APIs, events, RPA and agents composable under common control.
Workflows that recover from failure on their own — long-running business processes that adapt, retry and recover without tickets.
Agents that execute the work: tool-using, policy-bounded, and fully logged for audit.
Reference mismatches detected and remediated with counterparty comms (STP up 25-40 points)

blocks.caption: Regimes shaping this capability
rows: counterparty credit and market risk model quality
ICT risk, incident reporting, resilience testing and third-party oversight obligations with supervisory scrutiny

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Banking & Financial Services level this capability reads as: assembles registry extracts, screening results and account history per file; analysts judge instead of gathering (refresh cycle time down 60-80%). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

Programs run on a fixed rhythm so progress is visible from week one. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
